subject: Clarify: non-learning commitment & prompt/response ownership for ClearPath pilot
messages:
From: Emily Torres <emily@clearpathhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com, legal@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot questions: non-learning commitment & prompt ownership

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ClearPath is excited to try Redwood for our patient triage pilot. Before we can sign the pilot SOW our legal and procurement teams raised a couple of items that need clarity:

1) No-learning / no-training commitment: we need a contractual commitment that data submitted during the pilot will not be used to improve Redwood models or otherwise be included in any training datasets.
2) Prompt/response ownership: we want to confirm that prompts submitted by ClearPath and the model responses are treated as our data (we need explicit language that ClearPath retains ownership and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights).
3) Subprocessor visibility: can you provide a list of subprocessors that will touch pilot data and the locations where data will be processed/stored?

Legal requested a DPA redline and an operational evidence pack (logs/audit path) that shows how Redwood enforces a no-train commitment in practice. Can you confirm what you can provide and who on your side can take point?

Thanks,
Emily Torres
Head of Product Ops, ClearPath Health

Hi Emily — great to hear ClearPath is ready to move forward. Short answers up front, detailed follow-ups below:

1) Contract: Redwood can commit to a pilot-scoped "no-model-improvement" clause (we typically avoid the term "no-train" in legal text and use operationally measurable language).
2) Ownership: prompts and generated outputs for pilot tenant data can be contractually scoped to remain ClearPath property; we can add explicit output-licensing language.
3) Subprocessors / residency: see the attached redline (ClearPath_DPA_redline_v1.docx) and our ops playbook (nolearn-ops-playbook.pdf) — both attached.

Kimberly (Privacy) and Jonas (Legal) are copied — they can confirm the exact clause language and what operational evidence we can commit to for the pilot. Aditya (SE) will be the technical lead for the pilot and will coordinate the onshore routing and KV-prefix isolation we discussed.

Proposed next steps:
- Legal: review attached DPA redline and provide one consolidated markup.
- Ops: we'll produce an evidence bundle (audit logs, K/V residency mapping, proof of model variant isolation) within 7 business days after contract execution.
- Procurement: once redlines are agreed, attach the PO and we can spin up dedicated pilot capacity in us-west with onshore telemetry.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call today if helpful.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Emily — thanks for outlining the asks. A few clarifications from Privacy/Compliance and what we can commit to operationally for a pilot:

- Wording: we recommend DPA language that says "Redwood will not use Customer Data for model improvement, model fine-tuning, or to create new model weights for any general-purpose models during the Pilot Term; Redwood will route Pilot Data to a segregated serving footprint and exclude Pilot Data from any training pipelines." That language maps cleanly to operational controls we can prove.

- Evidence: we can provide a scoped evidence pack including:
  * Audit logs showing request IDs and routing to the segregated pool
  * Configuration snapshots proving model variant isolation and kernel selection flags
  * Timestamped proof of KV cache eviction policies for pilot tenant data
  * Subprocessor inventory with processing locations (we'll mark the pilot subprocessors and whether they are onshore)

- Telemetry: we can exclude pilot request telemetry from our central training telemetry stream and provide a signed attestation. Note: product telemetry for platform health (latency/metrics) will still flow to our monitoring systems but will be redacted/aggregated and excluded from training pipelines.

- Exceptions: we will flag any legal exceptions where we rely on telemetry for safety/regulatory reasons (e.g., PII detection that uses ephemeral models). We'll document those explicitly.

Operational ask for ClearPath: confirm whether you want onshore-only processing (us-only) or US + EU fallback. For the pilot we'll prioritize us-only unless you request otherwise.

I'll follow with a short ops checklist that Aditya can use during onboarding.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Lead, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Emily / team — quick legal note based on the redline you shared and Kim's operational suggestions. High level: we can accept a pilot-limited non-improvement commitment but propose the following edits for clarity and to limit operational risk: 

1) Replace the informal term "no-train" with a defined term in the DPA: "No Model Improvement from Customer Data" means Customer Data will not be used to update weights or augment training corpora for models made generally available by Redwood during the Pilot Term.
2) Telemetry carve-out: allow Redwood to retain platform telemetry necessary for security, safety, and debugging (explicitly defined narrow scope) but require that telemetry flagged as "TrainingEligible=false" is not exported to any training pipelines.
3) Subprocessor clause: require advance notice (30 days) for any change to subprocessors that would have access to Pilot Data, with a short attestation window we can meet.

On ownership: we will add an Output & Prompt Ownership section that states Customer retains ownership of Customer Input and Output; Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide license to any derivative platform telemetry we generate for billing and analytics, but we will not assert ownership over prompt/response content.

I'll prepare proposed language and push an updated DPA redline by EOD tomorrow. Also putting a short summary of acceptable evidence types (logs, signed attestations, config snapshots) so procurement has clarity on acceptance criteria.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — that all sounds reasonable and much more concrete than where we started. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

- We prefer the "No Model Improvement from Customer Data" defined term — please include the explicit duration (Pilot Term) and a clause describing how long you will retain associated audit bundles (we expect 12 months after pilot end for our review).
- We accept the telemetry carve-out so long as telemetry used for platform operations is redacted of content and demonstrably marked not-training.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable. Please confirm any subprocessors that will have access during the pilot (we saw the attachments but need explicit names + regions).

I've attached our PO template to speed procurement; procurement@clearpathhealth.com is copied and will kick off once we have the final DPA redline and the PO reflects pilot dates and committed pilot capacity.

Can we target sign-off next Monday so we can begin onboarding the week of July 26?

Best,
